note: THE CANDIDATE RECORD'S SHAPE, AND THE TEXT THE MODEL IS SHOWN BEFORE IT
COMPOSES ONE (kogaki#1126).
WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR. `src/leg-schema.json` declares the shape of ONE
LEG; nothing declared the shape of the CANDIDATE the Legs hang from. So
the Candidate's own fields were carried by `input_shape` -- one sentence
naming keys -- and the one field that reaches the OWNER, the option the
Candidate gate renders, was a single free-prose string. Whether an option
read `Adversarial: the reader is handed ...` or as an unbroken paragraph
was the composing Model's habit on the day, and the Harness guaranteed
neither half.
THE MEASURED SHAPE, at the Candidate gate of
runs/brief/brief-2026-09-15T22-53-48-359Z. Three options rendered with the
whole of the reader experience plus the figure clause in the LABEL and the
bare record id -- `A`, `B`, `C` -- in the description column, because
`composeGateCall` shows an option's id where it carries no description of
its own. The id is a join key between the gate and adoption; it is not
content, and it told the owner nothing.
SO THE MODEL CHOOSES VALUES INSIDE A HARNESS-ENFORCED FORMAT (owner
decision 2026-09-09). The two halves the rendering wanted are two FIELDS --
`characteristic` and `reader_experience` -- and `assembleSelection` renders
them into the option's label and description. A format the Harness composes
from declared fields cannot be a habit that lapses.
IT IS READ TWICE, which is the property `src/leg-schema.json` exists for
and the reason this is a file rather than a longer sentence. The
path-composition state of the Brief workflow table renders it into the
judge's prompt, and `compose_path`'s own validator refuses against the same
field set -- so the text the Model composes against and the text the
refusal enforces are one text and cannot disagree.
THE LEDGER FIELDS ARE HERE FOR THE SAME REASON THE TWO RENDERING
FIELDS ARE (kogaki#1129). `obligations`, `coverage` and `unused` were named
in one prose sentence -- `compose_path`'s `input_shape` -- and in no
declaration, so the composing Model chose their key names and the code that
reads them bound different ones: `raised_at`/`owed`/`settled_at` against
`text`/`introduced_by`/`discharged_by`, `role` against `role_in_thesis`, an
array against an object. Two of the three misreadings were SILENT -- the
Candidate gate rendered every entry as undischarged, and the coverage
section would have said `(not stated by the composer)` of a role the
composer stated -- and the third refused at the Brief's final write, after
two gates and three judge calls, outside every re-ask window. A sentence
describes; a declaration binds, and these three are now declared.
IT DECLARES SHAPE AND MEANING, AND JUDGES NEITHER. A missing field, a blank
one, an over-long characteristic and two Candidates stating the same
characteristic are refused here. Whether the characteristic NAMES the path
well is judgment, and it is judged at path review like every other MUST of
the composition design.
SPEC REFERENCES IN THIS FILE (kogaki#902; one carrier, kogaki#982). The
rule these entries are written under lives in ONE place:
`src/SPEC-REFERENCES.md`. It is not restated here.
THE NAMES THIS FILE USES, and the spec each one names:
The Candidate gate
SPEC-draft-pipeline
The settled structure section
SPEC-draft-pipeline
Every MUST is judgment, and nothing becomes a lint
SPEC-draft-pipeline
what_a_candidate_is: A Candidate is ONE COMPOSED READER PATH: an ordered sequence of Legs
taking the reader from the Brief's Reader start to the adopted Thesis,
plus the reasoning it was composed with. Two or three are composed per
article and they DIFFER IN READER EXPERIENCE -- not in decoration, not in
wording, and not in which Strands they happen to name first.
THE OWNER CHOOSES BETWEEN THEM AT THE CANDIDATE GATE, and that is the one
surface a Candidate has. Two fields below are that surface:
`characteristic` names the path in a few words and `reader_experience`
explains it. Everything else a Candidate carries is read by the runtime.
The Candidate gate is where the count, the difference-in-experience rule
and the premise negation are defined.
the_option_format: THE HARNESS COMPOSES THE OPTION; THE MODEL FILLS ITS FIELDS. Neither half
of the rendering below is composed by the party that writes this record,
and a Candidate cannot change the shape by writing its prose differently.
`<n>` is the option's POSITION in the rendered set, numbered from 1. It is
not the `candidate_id`: the id is the join key the owner's answer resolves
through and it is never shown as content, which is the defect kogaki#1126
closes. The figure clause is the Harness's own sentence about how many
Legs carry a figure; nothing here writes it.
SO THE TWO FIELDS ARE WRITTEN FOR THEIR SEATS. A `characteristic` that is
a sentence does not fit a label, and a `reader_experience` that repeats the
characteristic wastes the only line the owner gets to read.

candidate_id.description: This Candidate's own id, unique within the composed set. It is the JOIN KEY the owner's answer at the Candidate gate resolves through, and it is never rendered to the owner as content -- not as a label, not as a description. Short and mechanical is right here (`A`, `B`, `C`); a value composed to be read is a value in the wrong field.

characteristic.description: A SHORT NAME FOR THIS PATH, in a few words -- `Adversarial`, `Disillusionment first`, `Construction from the substrate up`. It is what the owner scans, so it names the path's character rather than describing its content: no sentence, no trailing clause, no colon introducing an explanation, because the explanation is the next field and rendering both here would leave the description restating the label. Bounded at 48 characters, refused above it -- the bound is the label's seat in the selector rather than a style preference, and a characteristic that needs more than 48 characters is an explanation that has drifted up a field.

reader_experience.description: WHAT THE READER GOES THROUGH on this path, stated so the difference from the sibling Candidates is legible -- this is the axis Candidates differ on, and the difference must be stated to be selectable. It renders as the option's DESCRIPTION, with the figure clause appended by the Harness, so it is written as the explanation of the characteristic above and never as a repeat of it. Two Candidates stating the same reader experience are refused, folded, as are two stating the same characteristic: either the paths do not differ or they are one path presented twice.

legs.description: The ordered Reader Path itself. Every entry is a Leg, whose fields, their meanings and their refusals are declared in `src/leg-schema.json` -- rendered into this same prompt and enforced by `validateLegs`. Nothing about a Leg is restated here.

retired_keys.transition_continuity: RETIRED (kogaki#1247, owner decision 2026-10-04) and REFUSED BY NAME where `reasoning` carries it -- an internal variable the gate never read ('Is it essentially an internal variable? Please remove it.'). The Candidate's reasoning now carries only `leg_validity`.
retired_keys.thesis_closure: RETIRED (kogaki#1328, owner decision 2026-10-10) and REFUSED BY NAME where `reasoning` carries it -- the Brief's Thesis row of Closure is DERIVED from each Strand's `coverage.role_in_thesis` and handed to the Leg marked `reaches_target`, so a free-text account of how the path closes the Thesis has no reader. Say what each Strand does in the Thesis under `coverage` instead.

reasoning.description: The composition-time reasoning this Candidate was composed with, one non-blank string per key. It is the Candidate's gate evidence; adoption fills no default, so a blank value is refused here, inside the re-ask window, rather than at the write.

reader_start.description: The reader's STANCE when the path begins -- one `dimension: value` LINE per dimension, drawn from the Move library's own dimension set (knowledge, question, expectation, orientation, trust -- the Move library entry), NOT a knowledge state alone (kogaki#1176). GIVEN, NOT COMPOSED HERE (kogaki#1216, owner decision 2026-09-28): Reader start is a cold read authored ONCE per Brief at the `differentiation` state, from the Persona (the reader file the workflow table names) and the adopted Thesis, never from the Move any first Leg binds. It is rendered above this prompt's input marker as YOUR ASSIGNED DIFFERENTIATION and the Harness sets it on the Candidate from the differentiation record; a value composed here is overwritten by that record and never read. It IS your first Leg's before-state (kogaki#1325): write no `reader_state_before` on any Leg -- the Harness derives each Leg's before-state as the previous Leg's `reader_state_after`, and the first Leg's as this Reader start, and a Leg carrying the field is refused by name. Bind an opening Move whose `before` requires nothing this Reader start does not hold. It is a line-per-dimension shape, not `moves_you_may_bind`'s own `before`/`after` shape verbatim -- a Move's `before`/`after` folds its dimensions into one paragraph, and a dimension's value there is ordinary prose free to carry any punctuation (kogaki#1211).

coverage.type: object keyed by selected Strand id
coverage.description: WHAT EACH SELECTED STRAND DOES IN THE THESIS, on this path. An OBJECT whose KEYS are the Strand ids of the Brief's closed set -- `L1`, `L2` -- and whose value carries `role_in_thesis`, one non-blank string. The Brief's Strand coverage section renders that string beside the Strand's derived placement, so a value under any other key renders as `(not stated by the composer)` beside a Strand the path in fact placed. An absent `coverage` is the empty object and every placed Strand renders unstated; a key naming a Strand outside the closed set is ignored by the render and refused here, because the set closed at mint and a Brief never fetches.

obligations.description: THE LEG HALF OF THE OBLIGATIONS LEDGER (kogaki#1151, kogaki#1529, SPEC-draft-pipeline "Obligations"): a promise the path makes to the reader that a later Leg must keep. Every entry is an object carrying `item` -- the list of one or more one-line items, each a term or a question the raising Leg leaves unexplained, in the order it names them, naming none twice; the retired `kind`, `text` and `term` are refused by name (kogaki#1568) --, `raised_by` (the `leg_id` of the Leg that raises it), `owed_by` (the `leg_id`s of the Legs that keep it, each AFTER `raised_by`, in path order; an explanation may span several) and EXACTLY ONE of `discharged_by` (the `leg_id` of the Leg that keeps the promise -- the LAST Leg in `owed_by`) or `conceded_by` (the `leg_id` of the Leg whose prose tells the reader it is left open -- the raising Leg or one in `owed_by`). Every id names a Leg OF THIS CANDIDATE and is refused otherwise. AN ENTRY CARRYING NEITHER TERMINAL FIELD, OR BOTH, IS REFUSED, naming the row -- "unresolved" is not a state this ledger can hold. That is exactly why the key names bind: a ledger the runtime cannot read is scored as wholly open and the owner is shown a confident number over a record nothing understood (kogaki#1129). An absent `obligations` is the empty ledger, which is a statement and not an omission. A MOVE YOUR LEG BINDS MAY RAISE A SLOT: where its `obligation` (in `moves_you_may_bind`) names an item it leaves unexplained, fill the slot with ONE row -- `item`, what THIS article leaves unexplained at that Leg, in the article's own words, one entry per slot item in the slot's order (the slot's `items` are the Move's general template and are never copied; a row whose count is not the slot's `count` is refused naming both, kogaki#1577), and the Legs that owe it, in the order the items were raised: one promise held open until the last of them is explained (kogaki#1549), never one row per item. NO OTHER ROW EXISTS (kogaki#1568): a promise the Strand material raises and no bound Move signals is not written -- bind a Move that carries it, or do not promise. A PROMISE THE PATH WILL NOT KEEP IS CONCEDED IN THE LEG THAT RAISES IT, unless a later Leg needs it open; the concession is made once and is not repeated at the close (owner decision 2026-09-30, kogaki#1232): `conceded_by` naming the same `leg_id` as `raised_by`, with an empty `owed_by`, is the ordinary case. `validateLegs` refuses a path carrying more than one `conceded_by` row; a Leg on which more than one row is open -- open meaning from a row's `raised_by` Leg up to, but not including, the Leg named in its `discharged_by` or `conceded_by`; and an open row any of whose `owed_by` Legs carries `opens_section`. A ROW WHOSE TERMINAL STATE IS `conceded_by` CARRIES THREE FURTHER FIELDS, required only there: `open` (what stays unresolved, in the composer's own words), `why_not_here` (why this Leg is not the one to close it) and `reader_keeps` (what the reader is left holding in its place, since a concession is not silence). A `discharged_by` row carries none of the three -- they describe what remains unresolved, and a row that keeps its promise leaves nothing unresolved to describe.

unused.description: THE DISCLOSURE FOR MATERIAL THIS PATH LEAVES UNPLACED. An OBJECT -- never an array -- whose KEYS are either a selected Strand id (`L2`) or that Strand's Journey material (`L2.journey`), and whose VALUE is the disclosure text: why the path leaves it unused. The claims rule's third move is omit the Leg, revise the path, or leave the Strand unused, never invention, and this field is where the third move is said out loud. An array carries no key to look the disclosure up under, so every unplaced Strand renders the Harness's default sentence and the composer's reason is lost; it is refused here rather than silently dropped. An absent `unused` is the empty object, and an unplaced Strand then discloses in the Harness's own words.

retired_fields.reader_target: RETIRED (kogaki#1225, owner decision 2026-09-29) and REFUSED BY NAME where a Candidate carries it. Reader target is DERIVED, not authored: it is the `reader_state_after` of the ONE Leg marked `reaches_target: true` (kogaki#1231, owner decision 2026-09-30, reversing #1225's last-Leg derivation -- see `reaches_target` and the three closing-Leg `path_rules` in src/leg-schema.json), whole, line for line, and the Brief renders that state under the `Reader target` heading the settled structure section names (src/assemble.mjs `readerFieldValues`). Authored apart from the Leg, it was a second statement of where the path leaves the reader that the Harness compared with nothing -- it checked only that the string was non-empty. Write where the path leaves the reader INTO the marked Leg's after-state, in the reader's own condition, and carry no field.
retired_fields.opening_question: RETIRED (kogaki#1216, owner decision 2026-09-28) and REFUSED BY NAME where a Candidate carries it. SINCE kogaki#1225 (owner decision 2026-09-29) NO Opening question is rendered at all: the `Opening question` heading is gone from the Brief, the fixed-points line is gone from the Leg Packet, and the first Leg's after-state is no longer required to carry a `question:` line. The first Leg already carries a before-state and an after-state, so a heading repeating its after-state question was a second Question inside Leg 1, rendered three times. Whatever question the opening leaves the reader holding belongs in the first Leg's after-state, in the reader's own words, and nowhere else.

what_is_judged_elsewhere: Nothing here is a lint over a judgment. Whether the characteristic names
the path WELL, whether the reader experience is the one the Legs actually
produce, and whether the three Candidates differ in a way worth choosing
between are judged at path review. A refusal from this file always names a
SHAPE: a field absent, a field blank, a characteristic over its bound, or
two Candidates whose characteristic or reader experience fold to the same
Every MUST is judgment, and nothing becomes a lint -- which is the rule
this paragraph is an instance of.

note: THE BRIEF RECORD (kogaki#1328, owner decision 2026-10-10). `theses/<slug>/brief.yaml` is the Brief: one YAML
record the owner reads and every command after adoption reads, written by the mint and filled at adoption
from the Candidate the owner selected. It is not composed by the judge reading this file -- it is declared
here because most of it is copied from the Candidate record above, and src/compose.mjs reads this key set
to refuse a record carrying any other key. A key below marked `filled_at: adoption` is `null` until the
Candidate is adopted; a Brief with a null key is a template, and /draft refuses it naming the key.
Each reader state is a five-key map (knowledge, question, expectation, orientation, trust) written once
per boundary: `reader_start` before the first Leg, then each Leg's `reader_state_after`; a Leg's
before-state is the state written before it. No line of the file is longer than 120 characters.
brief_record.header: A brief is the working plan for one article: the served material (Strands) the owner settled on, and the composition fields -- thesis, Reader Path, coverage, obligations -- filled in as composition proceeds. It is the durable document a drafting sitting resumes from. A key reading null is still awaiting composition.

slug.description: The Brief's name, which is also its directory under theses/.

compose_path.description: The path of the reader file (the Persona) the Reader start is authored from and the Packet reads its prose rules from (kogaki#1262).

strands.caption: The Strand set is closed at mint. Adding a Strand is your act, taken by going back through Terrain; a Brief never reaches for material on its own.
strands.description: The closed set the article may draw on, in the order it was settled: each entry's `id` (L1, L2, ...), its `slug`, its served `cite` at the content hash, its `journey_cite` where its served record carries Journey material, or `journey_uncited` where a Journey exists that the served record carries no cite for.

thesis.caption: The claim this article makes. You adopted it when the Brief was named; it is composed from the settled Strands and never invented.
thesis.description: The adopted Thesis, verbatim. The Draft's title is this text.

defined_terms.caption: The words this article gives a meaning to, and the words it uses as the reader already knows them. Written once, when the Brief was named; a word marked defined is used only after the leg that introduces it.
defined_terms.description: Every noun of the Thesis and of each Strand's claim, one entry per term (one or more words, in the form an `introduces` entry's `term` takes), each with `class` `defined` -- used in a sense this article gives it -- or `ordinary` -- used in the sense the reader already holds. Written once by the mint and never again (kogaki#1331). Composition refuses a `defined` term in a claim, a waypoint's point or a heading before the Leg whose `introduces` carries it. It lives in the Brief and ends there: nothing of it reaches the Packet. A Brief minted before the field carries none and defines nothing.

renderings.caption: The source's own words this article does not keep, each with the plain phrase it uses instead. A word not listed here keeps the source's wording.
renderings.description: The renderings record (kogaki#1494, owner decision 2026-10-21): one entry per term of the served material the article will not keep, `term` the served word and `as` the plain phrase the article uses in its place. Composed once at the `differentiation` state, before any reader-path unit runs, from the settled Strands and the Defined Terms (the `renderings_unit` row of src/brief-workflow.json); every reader-path unit composes under it and the Path Review judges each claim and point recoverable from its served material under it. Written into the Brief at adoption, beside the Reader Path composed under it; it is not a slot, so a Brief adopted before the field carries none and renders nothing. A term an `introduces` entry carries is refused here at adoption: `introduces` carries only terms the article keeps.

reader_start.caption: Where the reader stands before the article.
reader_start.description: The reader's state before the first Leg, as a five-key map -- given by the differentiation record and carried on the adopted Candidate.

reader_target.caption: Where the article leaves them: the state after the Leg named here.
reader_target.description: The `leg_id` of the one Leg marked `reaches_target`; the Reader target is that Leg's `reader_state_after`, written there once.

reader_path.caption: The ordered legs the article walks. Each leg starts from the state the one before it ends in.
reader_path.description: The adopted Candidate's Legs, in order, each with the fields src/leg-schema.json declares, its `reader_state_after` as a five-key map, and no `reader_state_before`.

strand_coverage.caption: Per settled Strand: which legs use it, and the part it plays in the claim. Counted after composition, never declared ahead of it.
strand_coverage.description: One entry per Strand of the closed set: `used_by_legs` derived from the Legs' materials and `role_in_thesis` from the Candidate's coverage, or `unplaced` with the Candidate's disclosure.

journey_coverage.caption: Per Strand carrying Journey material: the legs that place it, or why it was left out.
journey_coverage.description: One entry per Journey-bearing Strand: `placed_by` derived from the Legs' journeys, or `omitted` with the disclosure; an empty list where no settled Strand carries Journey material.

obligations.caption: An obligation is a promise the prose makes to the reader that a later passage must keep: a question raised, or a term named here and explained later. Each row names the leg that raises it and the legs that owe it, and ends kept or conceded by the leg that closes it. The Thesis itself is closed by the leg named under reader target, from the coverage above.
obligations.description: The Candidate's obligations ledger (kogaki#1529): each row's `item` list, `raised_by`, `owed_by`, and exactly one of `discharged_by` or `conceded_by`, a conceded row carrying `open`, `why_not_here` and `reader_keeps`. The Thesis row is derived, never written here.

tradeoffs.caption: What adopting this path gave up.
tradeoffs.description: `reader_experience`, the adopted Candidate's own; `gave_up` where the Candidate states its tradeoffs; `opening` where the run counted the Moves that could open from the Reader start.

bridged.caption: What the composer inserted to carry the reader across a gap, and on what reasoning.
bridged.description: `bridges`, the disclosure of every gap the path bridged, or the statement that none was.

defined_terms_record.note: THE MINT'S ONE JUDGED RECORD (kogaki#1331): the `defined_terms_unit` row of src/brief-workflow.json asks for it, and src/compose.mjs `definedTermsRefusal` refuses an entry against the same two fields. The mint writes `defined_terms` into the Brief from it, and nothing else reads it.

fields.defined_terms: a list, one entry per noun of the Thesis and of each Strand claim the input carries: `term` (one or more words, exactly as they occur in that text, in the form an `introduces` entry's `term` takes, so `non-member fallback` is one term) and `class`, one of `defined` (this article gives the word a sense the reader does not already hold -- a word used in a CI-specific or article-specific sense is `defined` even when it is everyday English) or `ordinary` (the reader already holds the sense the article uses). No other key, no prose, no term twice, and no term that occurs whole-word in neither the Thesis nor a claim.

renderings_record.note: THE DIFFERENTIATION STATE'S SECOND JUDGED RECORD (kogaki#1494, owner decision 2026-10-21): the `renderings_unit` row of src/brief-workflow.json asks for it before the Differentiation record, and src/compose.mjs `renderingsRefusal` refuses an entry against the same two fields. Every reader-path unit receives it, the Path Review's recoverability entry reads it, and adoption writes it into the Brief as `renderings`.

fields.renderings: a list, one entry per term of the Strand claims in the input that the article will NOT keep: `term` (one or more words, exactly as they occur in a claim, in the form an `introduces` entry's `term` takes) and `as` (the plain phrase the article uses in its place, in the article's language). A term absent from the list keeps the served word; a term the Thesis carries is kept, because the Thesis is the article's title. No other key, no prose, no term twice, no entry whose `as` is its own term, no term that occurs whole-word in no claim, and no term the Thesis carries. An empty list is a record in which the article keeps every served word.
